# **Deterministic Image-to-Terrain Pipeline for Latticewake**

A deterministic image-to-terrain pipeline for Latticewake in late 2026 requires a hard architectural boundary between SwiftUI document management, Apple-assisted image decoding, portable C++20 offline DSP preparation, and a lock-free real-time audio callback. Under this design, an imported fractal or photograph remains intact on disk and in UI coordinates as a registered visual source plane, while a background preparation worker decodes, color-normalizes, decomposes, and extracts periodic 2048-sample harmonic mipmap banks into an immutable render plan. Consistent with established real-time audio engineering practice, the C++20 audio callback performs zero image decoding, zero FFT planning or memory allocation, zero mutex locking, and zero disk I/O, consuming only pre-allocated wavetable buffers via atomic snapshot exchange1.  
For Latticewake's bounded first version (v1), the recommended architecture places the platform boundary immediately after canonical pixel ingest: Apple's ImageIO (CGImageSource), Core Graphics, and Accelerate (vImage) handle container parsing, EXIF orientation normalization, ICC color conversion, and Lanczos-5 downsampling into a canonical 512×512 linear-light RGBA float32 grid, whereas a portable C++20 DSP core compiled with \-ffp-contract=off and \-fno-fast-math executes all terrain analysis, periodic seam removal, trajectory slicing, and mipmap FFT generation4. No independent public benchmark comparing ImageIO/vImage, Metal compute, and portable CPU pipelines specifically for offline wave-terrain generation on macOS 26 Tahoe or macOS 27 Golden Gate was found in current reference literature; accordingly, this split prioritizes cross-architecture numerical determinism and SwiftUI responsiveness over raw GPU throughput while keeping the analysis backend swappable.  
Targeting macOS in November 2026 also introduces concrete OS and SDK constraints. According to Wikipedia and Parallels release coverage, macOS 26 Tahoe was the final release supporting Intel Macs, while macOS 27 Golden Gate—announced at WWDC on June 8, 2026 and released September 14, 2026—runs exclusively on Apple silicon and is the last release with full Rosetta 2 support10 (with point release 27.2.1 reported by MacRumors on November 9, 202612). On the 27 SDKs, Apple's developer documentation and release notes deprecate FileDocument and ReferenceFileDocument in favor of the Document protocol with asynchronous DocumentReader and DocumentWriter types13, and deprecate MTLCompileOptions.fastMathEnabled in favor of mathMode (MTLMathMode.safe or .fast) and mathFloatingPointFunctions16. Addressing both API transitions in v1 prevents immediate technical debt.

## **Apple-Native vs Portable CPU Analysis Backends**

**Fact:** Apple provides three primary native imaging and compute frameworks on macOS: ImageIO (CGImageSource) for container decoding and metadata inspection19; Core Graphics (CGImage) and Accelerate (vImage and vDSP) for color-managed bitmaps, Lanczos resampling, and 2D FFTs6; and Metal compute for GPU execution17. ImageIO reports supported container Uniform Type Identifiers dynamically via CGImageSourceCopyTypeIdentifiers() and exposes orientation, pixel dimensions, color models, and embedded ICC profile metadata via CGImageSourceCopyProperties before full pixel decoding23. Within Accelerate, vImageBuffer\_InitWithCGImage converts Core Graphics images into vImage\_Buffer storage, though Accelerate engineers have noted that implicit color-space and pixel-format conversions can dominate execution time depending on the source image format6. Accelerate's 2D FFT workflows also require expensive FFTSetup initialization that Apple's documentation advises creating once and reusing across calls21.  
**Fact:** On the GPU side, Metal's MTLMathMode.fast permits floating-point optimizations that may violate the IEEE 754 standard17, and GPU shader compilation can vary across OS generations (for example, an open-source macOS ML project reported Metal engine shader compilation failures on macOS 14 and 15 that did not reproduce on macOS 2628). On the CPU side, Clang compiles ARM64 (Apple silicon NEON) with \-ffp-contract=on by default, forming fused multiply-add (FMA) instructions within expressions, whereas baseline x86-64 builds without native FMA leave those operations uncontracted8. A 2026 cross-architecture quantization reproducibility study (arXiv:2610.19498) confirmed that disabling contraction (-ffp-contract=off) aligned ARM64 and x86-64 quantization kernels bit-for-bit on most models, while still exposing hardware-dependent edge cases such as 0/0 rounding residuals in all-zero blocks8. Similarly, standard libm transcendental functions such as hypot can diverge across glibc, musl, ARM64, and x86-64, leading deterministic audio engines to restrict math calls to basic IEEE 754 arithmetic plus floorf, fabsf, and sqrtf29.

| Backend Option | Role in Pipeline | Determinism and Portability | Strengths | Primary Risks and Tradeoffs |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| ImageIO (CGImageSource) | Container parsing, metadata, decode19 | High within an OS release; Apple-only | Supports standard, HDR, and RAW formats via OS-reported UTIs; safe pre-decode bounds19 | Lossy codec updates across macOS releases can alter least-significant pixel rounding |
| Core Graphics (CGImage / CGContext) | ICC color management and bitmap layout26 | Moderate; relies on Apple color management | Handles RGB, Gray, CMYK, Lab, and indexed images cleanly24 | Implicit 8-bit quantization or premultiplied rounding if float32 targets are omitted |
| Accelerate (vImage / vDSP) | Geometric resampling and 2D FFTs7 | Apple-only; SIMD behavior depends on Apple framework | Lanczos-3 default and Lanczos-5 (kvImageHighQualityResampling); optimized 2D FFTs7 | vImageBuffer\_InitWithCGImage hides color conversions; FFT setup cost requires caching21 |
| Metal Compute | Parallel 2D filtering and PDEs | Low cross-GPU bit-exactness; requires MTLMathMode.safe16 | High throughput on large (\>16 MP) buffers | Shader compile variance across OS versions28; unnecessary complexity for 512×512 grids |
| Portable C++20 CPU | Terrain math, Moisan decomposition, orbital FFTs | High cross-architecture parity with \-ffp-contract=off \-fno-fast-math8 | Zero Apple coupling; identical DSP tests on macOS ARM64 and Linux/Windows x86-64 CI | Slower than GPU/vImage on multi-megapixel images if not explicitly SIMD-tuned |

**Recommendation:** Adopt a hybrid boundary for v1: run ImageIO, Core Graphics, and vImage Lanczos-5 exclusively in a thin macOS ingest adapter to produce a bounded, canonical 512×512 linear-light RGBA float32 grid (4.0 MiB), and execute all downstream terrain extraction, periodic decomposition, and wavetable generation inside portable C++20. Persist the SHA-256 hash of that canonical grid in project metadata so future OS codec updates cannot silently alter an existing project's sound unless the user explicitly triggers a re-import.  
**Unresolved Tradeoff:** Resampling from source dimensions to 512×512 inside Apple's vImage (Lanczos-5) versus inside C++20 trades strict cross-platform source-to-terrain bit-exactness for Apple-silicon speed and mature ICC/color handling. Because Latticewake is macOS-native in 2026 with a portable C++20 engine, terminating Apple framework dependencies at the 512×512 canonical buffer keeps the C++20 synthesis core completely portable while leveraging ImageIO's security-hardened container decoders. Metal compute is unnecessary for 512×512 offline analysis and should be deferred unless a future version adds real-time GPU-driven procedural terrain synthesis.

## **Bounded First-Version Import and Terrain Analysis**

Every stage of the v1 ingest and analysis pipeline separates verified system facts from bounded design recommendations.

### **Formats, Dimensions, Memory Limits, Orientation, and Color Space**

**Fact:** Uncompressed pixel buffer memory grows quadratically with edge length: at 1024×1024 (1.05 MP), RGBA8 requires 4.0 MiB, RGBA16F 8.0 MiB, and RGBA32F 16.0 MiB; at 4096×4096 (16.78 MP), RGBA8 requires 64.0 MiB and RGBA32F 256.0 MiB; and at 8192×8192 (67.11 MP), RGBA8 reaches 256.0 MiB while RGBA32F reaches 1024.0 MiB32. ImageIO provides kCGImageSourceAllowableTypes to restrict accepted UTIs, kCGImagePropertyOrientation to inspect intended display orientation, kCGImageSourceCreateThumbnailWithTransform (default kCFBooleanFalse) with kCGImageSourceThumbnailMaxPixelSize to decode bounded, correctly rotated bitmaps, kCGImageSourceShouldAllowFloat for floating-point output, and CGImageSourceGetPrimaryImageIndex to select the primary frame in HEIF containers5.  
**Recommendation:** Restrict v1 imports via kCGImageSourceAllowableTypes to standard still-image UTIs (such as PNG, JPEG, TIFF, HEIF/HEIC primary image, and WebP, intersected with CGImageSourceCopyTypeIdentifiers() at runtime19), deferring camera RAW and multi-channel OpenEXR to v2. Before decoding pixels, inspect kCGImagePropertyPixelWidth and kCGImagePropertyPixelHeight24. Enforce a hard ingest ceiling of 8192 px maximum axis length and 67.11 MP total (1024.0 MiB RGBA32F ceiling32); reject larger files or require explicit user downscale confirmation, and never decode an oversized source directly into full-resolution RGBA32F when a bounded working copy suffices. Decode a UI preview plane capped at 2048 px long edge via kCGImageSourceCreateThumbnailFromImageAlways, kCGImageSourceThumbnailMaxPixelSize, and kCGImageSourceCreateThumbnailWithTransform \= true5, while converting the image into a square **512×512 canonical terrain buffer** (1.0 MiB per planar float32 field, 4.0 MiB for RGBA32F).  
**Recommendation:** Bake the EXIF orientation from kCGImagePropertyOrientation into the canonical bitmap at ingest so UI overlay coordinates and C++20 terrain coordinates ![][image1] match identically5. Convert all input color models (RGB, Gray, CMYK, Lab, and indexed palettes flagged by kCGImagePropertyIsIndexed) via Core Graphics into **unpremultiplied linear-light sRGB** float3224. Multiply RGB by alpha over black (treating opaque/missing alpha as 1.0) and sanitize any NaN or ±Inf values from float TIFFs to 0.0. Using linear light prevents sRGB gamma encoding from crushing shadow terrain gradients and artificially exaggerating highlight slopes.

### **Resampling and Image-Derived Terrain Fields**

**Fact:** Accelerate's vImage defaults to Lanczos-3 interpolation and uses Lanczos-5 when kvImageHighQualityResampling is enabled, preserving fine detail while suppressing resampling aliasing7. In wave terrain literature, Borgonovo and Haus (1986) and subsequent research model a 2D surface ![][image2] as an elevation matrix whose maxima/minima govern intensity and whose geometric complexity shapes audio timbre along a scanning trajectory34.  
**Recommendation:** Resample the linear-light bitmap onto the square 512×512 canonical grid using vImage with kvImageHighQualityResampling (Lanczos-5) and zero-padding-free backing storage (rowBytes \= width \* 4 \* sizeof(float))7. Expose a deterministic aspect-handling option—**Center Crop** (default, filling the periodic square with fractal detail without artificial flat margins) or **Fit/Pad** (letterboxed against zero). Inside C++20, derive four planar float32 terrain fields (1.0 MiB each at 512×512) from the canonical RGBA32F grid:

| Terrain Field | Mathematical Definition | Sonic / Modulation Interpretation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Luminance (![][image3]) | ![][image4] | Primary surface elevation ![][image5] mapping brightness directly to waveform amplitude |
| RGB Channel / Opponent (![][image6]) | Selectable R, G, B, or ![][image7] / ![][image8] | Secondary timbral layer for chromatic fractals whose luminance is relatively uniform |
| Gradient Magnitude (![][image9]) | ![][image10] via periodic central differences | Local slope steepness; drives harmonic richness, orbital eccentricity, or wavefolder depth |
| Edge Density (![][image11]) | Separable 7-tap Gaussian blur of ![][image9] | Smoothed local textural complexity; modulates frame index or trajectory spread without clicks |

### **Normalization, Periodic Tiling, Cancellation, and Reproducibility**

**Fact:** Mitsuhashi (1982) established that wave terrain functions over ![][image12] and ![][image13] should maintain continuity in both value and first-order partial derivatives to avoid harsh waveform discontinuities33. Ordinary photographs and cropped fractals rarely wrap seamlessly at borders, producing edge-step impulses whenever a periodic trajectory crosses the image boundary. Lionel Moisan (2011), *"Periodic plus Smooth Image Decomposition"* (*Journal of Mathematical Imaging and Vision* 39(2): 161–179), separates an image into a periodic component free of wrap-around edge artifacts and a smooth boundary-jump residual36.  
**Recommendation:** Provide three deterministic seam-handling modes in v1, defaulting to **Moisan Periodic Decomposition** (keeping the periodic component), alongside **Mirror-Symmetric Tile** (2×2 reflection guaranteeing ![][image14] border continuity at doubled spatial period) and **Raw Wrap** (for genuinely seamless procedural textures). Moisan decomposition preserves crisp interior fractal edges while mathematically eliminating border wrap discontinuities without edge-fade halos or mirror-symmetry harmonic doubling36. Normalize each resulting field by computing mean ![][image15] and variance ![][image16] in a fixed row-major double-precision accumulator: if ![][image17] (e.g., uniform solid color), flag the plane as silent/degenerate rather than magnifying 8-bit quantization noise; otherwise center to zero mean and scale peak magnitude into ![][image18] (with optional 0.1%–99.9% outlier clamping off by default).  
**Recommendation:** Execute all background ingest and C++20 terrain preparation inside a Swift Task linked to a C++20 std::stop\_token, polling stop\_requested() before decode, after resize, per 2D FFT/Moisan step, and every 8 wavetable frames. Coalesce rapid UI edits in a "latest-wins" slot so cancelled intermediate runs never touch the live audio plan. For bit-exact reproducibility across Apple silicon and x86-64 test runners, compile the C++20 library with \-ffp-contract=off \-fno-fast-math, pin IEEE 754 round-to-nearest-even, avoid parallel non-associative floating-point reductions, guard 0/0 divisions explicitly, and restrict math functions to IEEE-specified operations (floorf, fabsf, sqrtf)8.

| Pipeline Parameter | Bounded v1 Specification | Classification |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Accepted image formats | Standard still formats (PNG, JPEG, TIFF, HEIF primary frame, WebP) validated via kCGImageSourceAllowableTypes19 | Recommendation (bounded v1) |
| Dimension & memory cap | Max 8192 px edge, ≤67.11 MP (1024.0 MiB RGBA32F ceiling)32; UI plane capped at 2048 px | Fact (memory math) \+ Recommendation |
| Canonical analysis grid | 512×512 planar float32 (1.0 MiB/field, 4.0 MiB RGBA32F) via vImage Lanczos-57 | Fact (vImage/math) \+ Recommendation |
| Orientation & color | Apply kCGImagePropertyOrientation5; convert to unpremultiplied linear-light sRGB float32 | Recommendation |
| Seam & tiling mode | Moisan (2011) periodic component default36; Mirror-Tile and Raw Wrap optional | Fact (Moisan) \+ Recommendation |
| Determinism profile | C++20 compiled with \-ffp-contract=off \-fno-fast-math; fixed summation order; guarded 0/08 | Fact (FP behavior) \+ Recommendation |

## **Converting Terrain Fields into Pitch-Stable Periodic Tables**

**Fact:** Classic wave terrain synthesis (Gold 1978; Mitsuhashi 1982; Borgonovo & Haus 1986\) evaluates a 2D surface ![][image2] along a parametric trajectory ![][image19], where periodic orbital frequency sets pitch and terrain geometry determines harmonic spectrum33. Evaluating arbitrary 2D trajectories directly inside a real-time audio callback on unfiltered 2D pixels acts like nonlinear waveshaping/FM and folds harmonics above Nyquist (![][image20]) back into the audible spectrum—aliasing that cannot be removed by downstream filtering4. Meanwhile, Latticewake's current 8-voice engine reads interpolated 2048-sample 1D wavetables and morphs between two prepared Surface layers.  
**Recommendation:** Convert each 2D terrain field offline into an ordered bank of ![][image21] (configurable up to ![][image22]) periodic **2048-sample wavetable frames** sampled along deterministic closed trajectories across the 512×512 periodic surface, accompanied by a lightweight 64×64 float32 control grid of edge density/gradient values for slow control-rate modulation35. Three trajectory geometries link visual structure on the registered plane to pitch-stable audio: **Parallel Scanlines** (64 evenly spaced horizontal or angled slices across the periodic terrain), **Concentric Ellipses** (![][image23], ![][image24] expanding outward from the user's focal point ![][image25]33), and **Lissajous Orbits** (![][image26], ![][image27]33). Because every frame spans one exact closed period ![][image28] mapped onto 2048 samples, oscillator pitch tracks MIDI frequency cleanly regardless of terrain complexity.

### **DC Removal and Phase Alignment**

**Fact:** Arbitrary terrain slices generally carry non-zero DC offsets, and harmonic phase mismatches across wavetable frames or between two morphing layers cause constructive/destructive interference and crest-factor shifts (as illustrated in phase-alignment analysis tools such as Daqarta40).  
**Recommendation:** After cubic/Lanczos resampling of each raw closed trajectory to 2048 samples, perform a 2048-point real-to-complex FFT offline and **zero bin 0 (DC)** unconditionally across the base frame and all mipmap levels, guaranteeing residual DC below \-120 dBFS.  
**Unresolved Tradeoff (Phase Alignment):** Morphing between Surface A and Surface B presents a fundamental phase tradeoff:

> * **Zero-Phase / Minimum-Phase Alignment:** Setting harmonic phases to zero (cosine-symmetric) or minimum-phase eliminates phase cancellation during linear A/B morphs39, **but** concentrates energy at phase 0, giving distinct fractal slices a uniform high-crest "buzzy" waveform profile that visually diverges from the imported terrain.  
> * **Fundamental-Phase Circular Alignment:** Rotating each frame in time so harmonic 1 sits at phase 0 preserves relative higher-harmonic phase relationships and keeps the 1D waveform visually recognizable as a slice of the image while preventing frame-to-frame phase drift, **but** allows partial comb-like dips when morphing between two unrelated Surface A and B images.**Recommendation:** Default to **Fundamental-Phase Alignment** to preserve visual-sonic fidelity, and provide a per-Surface **"Zero-Phase Morph Lock"** toggle for sound designers who prioritize smooth cross-layer morphs.

### **Table Banks, Harmonic Mipmaps, Interpolation, and Aliasing**

**Fact:** A 2048-sample wavetable spans up to 1024 harmonics4. At sample rate ![][image29] and fundamental ![][image30], using a conservative 0.45 \* fs anti-alias guardband (19,845 Hz at 44.1 kHz, 21,600 Hz at 48 kHz, 43,200 Hz at 96 kHz), maximum safe harmonic counts ![][image31] shrink sharply at higher MIDI notes32. Nigel Redmon (EarLevel Engineering) notes that power-of-two 2048-sample tables work well from 20 Hz upward when paired with topFreq-tagged bandlimited mipmap tables4. However, standard audio resampling analysis (mp3-tech.org DSP documentation) emphasizes that octave-spaced mipmapping alone does not eliminate aliasing introduced by the *interpolator* itself41. Olli Niemitalo (2001) reported modified SNR figures for the **4-point, 3rd-order Hermite** interpolator of 23.5 dB at 2× oversampling, 44.2 dB at 4×, 64.0 dB at 8×, 83.1 dB at 16×, and 101.8 dB at 32× (noting that 6-point 5th-order Hermite reaches 31.0 dB to 155.4 dB; comparative tables and equations for linear, Lagrange, and B-spline interpolators were unavailable in the consulted excerpt)42. Similarly, the Neutone SDK paper (arXiv:2508.09126v1) describes 4-point cubic Hermite as offering the strongest quality-to-complexity tradeoff among zero-allocation polynomial interpolators43, while Välimäki et al. (2010) highlight low-order (order-3, 4-sample) polynomials for avoiding large windowed-sinc lookup tables44.

| MIDI 36 (65.41 Hz) | 303 | 330 | 660 | 256 | 4× | 44.2 dB42 |
| MIDI 48 (130.81 Hz) | 151 | 165 | 330 | 128 | 8× | 64.0 dB42 |

**Fact (Mipmap Memory Budgets):** Storing 11 octave-spaced mip bands (![][image32]) per frame in 32-bit float produces two memory profiles32:

> * **Uniform 2048-sample mips:** 5.50 MiB/layer (11.00 MiB for 2 layers) at 64 frames; 11.00 MiB/layer (22.00 MiB for 2 layers) at 128 frames; 22.00 MiB/layer (44.00 MiB for 2 layers) at 256 frames32.  
> * **Decimated mips (2048, 1024, ..., 16):** \< 2× base table size—1.01 MiB/layer at 64 frames; 2.02 MiB/layer at 128 frames; 4.03 MiB/layer at 256 frames32.

**Unresolved Tradeoff & Recommendation (Uniform vs Decimated Mips):** Decimated mipmaps save roughly 5.4× memory (2.02 MiB vs 11.00 MiB for two 64-frame layers), **but** shrinking upper-octave tables to 128, 64, or 16 samples pins every octave's table oversampling ratio near 1×–2×, where 4-point Hermite interpolation SNR drops toward 23.5 dB unless the audio callback runs 2×–4× real-time oversampling with a half-band decimator32. **Recommend uniform 2048-sample mip levels** (64 frames × 11 octave bands \= 5.50 MiB/layer, 11.00 MiB total for Surface A \+ Surface B) so that from Middle C (261.63 Hz) upward, the table itself provides ≥16× oversampling (≥83.1 dB Hermite SNR42) at native 1× callback sample rate with branchless modulo masking (& 2047). Note also that below \~130 Hz, 2×–8× table oversampling yields 23.5–64.0 dB Hermite SNR; if ultra-bright bass presets show audible interpolation imaging, upgrade to 6-point 5th-order Hermite (31.0 dB at 2×42) or add half-octave mip bands (k\_band \= 724, 512, 362...) in v2.  
**Recommendation (Offline Bandlimiting & Modulation Aliasing):** Generate each mip level offline by applying a 10% raised-cosine spectral taper below ![][image33] and zeroing bins above ![][image33] before inverse FFT4, avoiding Gibbs ringing on sharp fractal cliffs. In the callback, select the bracketing mip pair via topFreq4, evaluate **4-point cubic Hermite interpolation** along phase, and linearly crossfade across mip level, frame index, and Surface A/B. Crucially, as Redmon emphasizes, static mipmaps cannot prevent sideband aliasing if Latticewake applies audio-rate phase modulation (FM/PM) or phase distortion during lookup4; either attenuate FM/PD index progressively at high pitches (the DX7 roll-off technique4) or oversample the voice bus.

### **Smoothing, Clicks, Polyphonic Gain, Memory Limits, and Overload Behavior**

**Recommendation:** Smooth all real-time control inputs (Surface A/B morph, frame index, gain) per sample with a 5–15 ms one-pole filter or linear ramp to eliminate zipper noise. Never mutate an active SurfaceBank in place: publish newly prepared immutable render plans from the NRT thread via a lock-free single-producer/single-consumer (SPSC) queue1. When a new render plan arrives mid-note, either pin sounding notes to their start-of-note plan handle (reclaiming the old handle via a lock-free return queue back to the NRT thread once active voice reference counts reach zero) or execute a 10–20 ms voice-level crossfade from old plan to new plan.  
**Fact & Recommendation (Gain & Memory Ceiling):** For 8 voices, strict coherent worst-case summation requires 1/N \= 0.1250 (-18.06 dB), whereas uncorrelated summation requires 1/sqrt(N) \= 0.3536 (-9.03 dB)32. Set nominal per-voice trim to 0.25 (-12.04 dB, matching 4-voice coherent headroom32) followed by a zero-latency soft-saturating ceiling (tanh limiter) at \-0.5 dBFS on the master bus. Pre-allocate a **fixed memory pool** at engine boot holding 2 active \+ 2 staged SurfaceBank slots (4 × 5.50 MiB \= 22.00 MiB at 64 frames, capped at ≤88.00 MiB even if expanded to 256 frames32), guaranteeing zero heap activity during playback3.  
**Recommendation (Deterministic Overload Shedding):** Measure callback duration with Mach high-resolution timers against 0.75 × bufferDuration. If execution approaches deadline, step down cleanly without locks or dropped frames: first snap to single-mip lookup (skipping mip crossfading); second fall back from 4-point Hermite to linear phase interpolation; third limit polyphony from 8 to 4 voices via a 3 ms fade-out steal on the quietest voice; fourth freeze Surface A/B morph smoothing at block rate.

| Work Item | Offline Preparation (NRT Worker) | Real-Time Audio Callback |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Image decoding & sizing | ImageIO decode, EXIF transform, linear sRGB, Lanczos-5 resize to 512×5125 | Never executed |
| Terrain & seam fields | Luminance, RGB opponent, gradient, edge density; Moisan decomposition36; normalization | Never executed |
| Wavetable & mipmap build | 2048-pt orbital slicing, FFT DC removal, phase alignment, 11-level iFFT4 | Never executed |
| Render plan exchange | Pre-allocate pool; push immutable SurfaceBank handle; free retired plans1 | Atomic SPSC pop of new handle; push retired handle to NRT free queue |
| Voice synthesis | N/A | Parameter smoothing, topFreq mip selection4, 4-pt Hermite lookup, A/B morph, \-12.04 dB mix \+ soft ceiling |

## **Asset Provenance, Project Packaging, and Missing-Asset Recovery**

**Recommendation (Hashes & Provenance Metadata):** Record three SHA-256 digests in each Surface layer's JSON manifest: sourceFileSha256 (raw imported image bytes), canonicalGridSha256 (512×512 linear-light RGBA32F grid post-Apple ingest), and renderPlanSha256 (compiled float32 SurfaceBank binary). Pair these with providerId (e.g., "apple.imageio+vimage.lanczos5" and "latticewake.cpp20.ieee754"), macosVersion (e.g., "27.2.1"), engineSchemaVersion (1), compilerMathProfile ("ffp-contract-off-ieee754"), and complete analysisSettings (crop/fit, seam mode, trajectory type, focal center, frame count, phase mode, outlier clamping).  
**Fact & Recommendation (SwiftUI Packaging in 2026):** Because SwiftUI deprecates FileDocument and ReferenceFileDocument in the 27 SDKs, implement Latticewake's .lwake project as an @Observable class conforming to the Document protocol with async FileWrapperDocumentReader / FileWrapperDocumentWriter and explicit UndoManager registration13. Store the project as a directory FileWrapper package45 containing manifest.json, Assets/layerA.\* and Assets/layerB.\*, and Cache/layerA.terrain.bin \+ Cache/layerB.terrain.bin. Using a directory FileWrapper lets macOS rewrite only manifest.json during parameter edits without re-writing megabytes of binary wavetable caches45.  
**Unresolved Tradeoff (Embedded vs Linked Source Images):** Embedding full source images inside the .lwake package guarantees project portability across Macs but inflates project size for large fractals; storing security-scoped external bookmarks keeps .lwake lightweight but risks broken links. **Recommendation:** Default to embedding a lossless-compressed copy (or original file if ≤16 MiB) inside Assets/ with an optional "Reference external file" setting.  
**Recommendation (Missing-Asset & Corrupt-Cache Behavior):** On project load, verify Cache/\*.terrain.bin against renderPlanSha256 first; if valid, initialize the audio engine immediately in real time even if the source image is missing, showing a non-blocking "Source plane offline — playing from verified terrain cache" banner with a Relink action. If both the source image and cache are missing or fail hash checks, load a deterministic neutral fallback bank (pure 2048-sample fundamental sine at \-12.04 dB, zero DC) so the synthesizer never crashes or stalls audio startup.

## **Staged Implementation Plan, Failure Cases, and Validation**

> 1. **Stage 1 — Portable C++20 Terrain & Wavetable Core:** Implement 512×512 field extraction, Moisan decomposition, orbital slicing, 2048-point FFT DC removal, phase alignment, and 11-level mipmapping in C++20 compiled with \-ffp-contract=off \-fno-fast-math4. Verify bit-identical renderPlanSha256 digests on Apple silicon and x86-64 CI.  
> 2. **Stage 2 — Apple Ingest & SwiftUI Document Packaging:** Build the ImageIO \+ Core Graphics \+ vImage Lanczos-5 ingest adapter with kCGImageSourceAllowableTypes, orientation baking, std::stop\_token cancellation, and directory FileWrapper persistence under the 27 SDK Document protocol5.  
> 3. **Stage 3 — Lock-Free 8-Voice Real-Time Engine:** Integrate SPSC render-plan swapping1, 4-point Hermite lookup42, dual-mip crossfading, Surface A/B morphing, \-12.04 dB voice trim, and deadline-triggered overload shedding.  
> 4. **Stage 4 — Fuzzing, Sanitizer Stress Testing, and Listening Trials:** Fuzz malformed image headers, run 10-minute rapid-swap stress tests under Thread Sanitizer and Xcode Allocations, and execute structured human listening evaluations.

| Failure Case | Root Cause | Concrete Mitigation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Memory spike on \>67 MP file | Unbounded RGBA32F decode (\>1 GiB)32 | Check kCGImagePropertyPixelWidth/Height pre-decode; enforce 8192 px cap and thumbnail sizing5 |
| Noise amplification on flat image | Normalizing zero-variance terrain (![][image34]) | Gate on ![][image17] before scaling; emit silent/sine fallback flag |
| NaN / Inf poison in wavetable | Corrupted float TIFF pixel values5 | Clamp non-finite samples to 0.0 at ingest boundary before C++20 handoff |
| Loud pop on scene swap or note-on | Mid-cycle pointer overwrite or residual DC | Zero FFT bin 0; pin active voice handles or apply 15 ms crossfade1 |
| Worker backlog during UI scrub | Queuing redundant 512×512 analyses | Coalesce pending jobs ("latest-wins") \+ cancel via std::stop\_token |
| Audio glitch on RT thread | Mutex wait or free() inside callback2 | Wait-free SPSC reclamation queue back to NRT thread3 |

### **Objective Test Fixtures vs Human Listening Evaluation**

Automated DSP fixtures establish mathematical correctness and real-time reliability, whereas aesthetic quality requires human listening. Spectral similarity between an image's 2D FFT and an audio output spectrum must never be treated as an aesthetic verdict: an exact spectral match of noisy high-frequency image texture can still sound harsh, static, or musically unplayable.

| Synthetic Test Fixture | Property Verified | Objective Pass Threshold |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Uniform constant gray (0.5 linear) | DC removal & zero-variance guard | Peak output ≤ \-120 dBFS; zero NaN/Inf |
| Linear ramp with edge step | Moisan periodic seam removal36 | Edge jump reduced ≥40 dB vs raw wrap; zero boundary impulse |
| Binary 2×2 checkerboard / step | Mipmap aliasing (20 Hz–12 kHz sweep @ 44.1 kHz) | Folded aliases ≤ \-70 dBFS above 261.63 Hz under 4-point Hermite32 |
| Concentric zone plate | Lanczos-5 resampling & gradient/edge maps7 | Zero moiré foldback; edge-density tracks radial frequency monotonically |
| Cross-arch deterministic build | Reproducibility (-ffp-contract=off \-fno-fast-math)8 | Identical renderPlanSha256 across 100 runs and ARM64 vs x86-64 CI |
| 8-voice chord \+ 20 Hz Surface swap | Clicks, headroom, RT safety2 | Master peak ≤ \-0.5 dBFS; 0 allocations, locks, or xruns over 10 minutes |

Four perceptual questions cannot be answered by objective test thresholds and must be evaluated through blind listening sessions with musicians and sound designers: whether **Luminance vs RGB Opponent vs Gradient Magnitude** mappings feel intuitively connected to the visual source plane; whether **Moisan periodic decomposition** removes edge clicks without softening the perceived character of sharp geometric fractals relative to Mirror-Tiling; whether **Fundamental-Phase Alignment vs Zero-Phase Morph Lock** provides a better musical tradeoff between timbral authenticity and smooth Layer A/B crossfading; and whether **Edge-Density modulation** adds expressive playability or distracting busyness across sustained 8-voice polyphony.
